correctness.rationale: The exact source update is \(x_2=x_1[1-(1-\beta_1)h\widehat\eta_1]\). The raw first rate is proportional to \(1/|x_1|\), so clipping realizes the full interval \([\ell_1,u_1]\). Universal objective nonincrease is therefore equivalent to the sharp endpoint condition \((1-\beta_1)h u_1\le2\). When it fails, the upper-clipped neighborhood and its fixed amplification follow by direct substitution.

value.rationale: AdaBound's defining mechanism is to replace extreme Adam rates by dynamic clipping bounds. The theorem identifies exactly when that upper bound is safe on the canonical scalar quadratic, shows that the recommended high-beta2 schedule can permit a large expanding first step, and separates a finite clipped rate from a curvature-compatible clipped rate.
